solution: One year's simple interest is \(11076 - 10650 = 426\). Five years' interest is \(5 \times 426 = 2130\), so the principal is \(10650 - 2130 = 8520\), that is Rs. 8,520.
Nine months is \(\frac{3}{4}\) of a year. The interest is \(6000 \times \frac{12}{100} \times \frac{3}{4} = 540\), that is Rs. 540.
Three years at \(10\%\) multiply the principal by \((1.1)^3 = 1.331\). So the principal is \(\frac{14641}{1.331} = 11000\), that is Rs. 11,000.
For 2 years the difference is \(P \left(\frac{R}{100}\right)^2 = 8000 \times (0.1)^2 = 80\). The difference is Rs. 80.

subtopic: Simple Interest: Finding Principal, Rate or Time
solution: Four years at \(5\%\) add \(20\%\), so the amount is \(1.2\) times the principal. The principal is \(\frac{9000}{1.2} = 7500\), that is Rs. 7,500.
Quarterly compounding at \(4\%\) a year means \(1\%\) a quarter for 4 quarters. The amount is \(10000 \times (1.01)^4 \approx 10406.04\), so the interest is about Rs. 406.
The interest is \(\frac{25000 \times 6 \times 3}{100} = 4500\). The amount is \(25000 + 4500 = 29500\), that is Rs. 29,500.

Simple interest is Rs. 800 a year. Compound interest is Rs. 160 more, which is the interest on the first year's Rs. 800, so the rate is \(\frac{160}{800} \times 100 = 20\%\). The principal is \(\frac{800}{0.2} = 4000\), that is Rs. 4,000.
Eighteen months is \(1.5\) years, so the interest is \(7000 \times \frac{6}{100} \times 1.5 = 630\). The amount is Rs. 7,630.
The amount is \(5000 \times (1.1)^3 = 6655\). The compound interest is \(6655 - 5000 = 1655\), that is Rs. 1,655.

solution: Five years at \(7\%\) give \(35\%\) of the principal as interest. The principal is \(\frac{1750}{0.35} = 5000\), that is Rs. 5,000.

solution: Three years at \(7\%\) give \(21\%\) of the sum as interest. If that is Rs. 2,100, the sum is \(\frac{2100}{0.21} = 10000\), that is Rs. 10,000.

subtopic: Simple Interest: Finding Principal, Rate or Time
solution: One year's simple interest is \(9680 - 8800 = 880\). Two years' interest is 1760, so the principal is \(8800 - 1760 = 7040\), that is Rs. 7,040.

Compound interest for 2 years at \(5\%\) is \((1.05)^2 - 1 = 10.25\%\) of the principal. Simple interest for 3 years at \(3\%\) is \(9\%\). The gap of \(1.25\%\) is Rs. 1,125, so the principal is \(\frac{1125}{0.0125} = 90000\), that is Rs. 90,000.
Half-yearly at \(10\%\) means \(5\%\) per half-year, and 1.5 years is 3 half-years. So the investment is \(\frac{18522}{(1.05)^3} = \frac{18522}{1.157625} = 16000\), that is Rs. 16,000.
Semi-annual compounding at \(8\%\) means \(4\%\) twice a year: \((1.04)^2 = 1.0816\). The effective annual rate is \(8.16\%\).

solution: Doubling means the interest equals the principal, that is \(100\%\) in 10 years. The rate is \(\frac{100}{10} = 10\%\) per annum.
